Solution 3 is correct, and Solutions 1 and 2 are not.

All three solutions agree that f'(θ) = i e^{iθ}(1+e^{iθ})², so |f'(θ)| = 2 + 2cos θ = 4cos²(θ/2). The total arc length of the curve is therefore 4π. That is the length of the whole curve, including the inner loop, not the perimeter of the enclosed region.

The curve self-intersects. At θ = 2π/3, f = ω + ω² + 1/3 = −1 + 1/3 = −2/3. At θ = 4π/3, f = ω² + ω + 1/3 = −2/3 as well. So the curve has an inner loop for θ in [2π/3, 4π/3], and the region R is bounded by the outer loop only.

The outer loop has length 2∫₀^{2π/3} 4cos²(θ/2) dθ = 4[θ + sin θ]₀^{2π/3} = 8π/3 + 2√3 ≈ 11.84.

Solutions 1 and 2 give 4π, which counts the inner loop as well. Solution 1's claim that the curve is simple is wrong, because it fails to see the self-intersection at −2/3. Solution 3's answer, 8π/3 + 2√3, matches the outer-loop length.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
